req.title: Sessions use secret key
req.statement: The system shall sign session cookies with the SECRET_KEY loaded from application config.

doc.reasoning: R-FLASKR-034 requires that session cookies are signed with the SECRET_KEY from application config. We test: (1) positive — app configured with a custom SECRET_KEY signs sessions so a valid login sets a signed session cookie and the session persists correctly; (2) negative — a client presenting a session cookie signed with a DIFFERENT secret key is rejected (session data not trusted, user treated as anonymous); (3) boundary — the default 'dev' SECRET_KEY is replaced when a custom key is supplied, and two apps with different keys cannot share sessions (cookie from one is invalid in the other). We also verify the exact HTTP status codes and that SECRET_KEY is actually read from config.

tests.name: test_session_signed_with_configured_secret_key_positive
preconditions: App created with TESTING=True and a known SECRET_KEY='test-secret-key-abc'
actions: Inspect response status and Set-Cookie header
GET / with the session cookie to confirm user is recognised
expected: Subsequent GET / returns HTTP 200 (session accepted, user logged in)
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path, 'SECRET_KEY': 'test-secret-key-abc'})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()

assert app.config['SECRET_KEY'] == 'test-secret-key-abc'

client = app.test_client()

def test_session_signed_with_configured_secret_key_positive():
    r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    cookie_header = r.headers.get('Set-Cookie', '')
    assert 'session=' in cookie_header
    r2 = client.get('/')
    assert r2.status_code == 200

tests.name: test_session_cookie_from_different_secret_key_rejected
preconditions: Two app instances created with DIFFERENT SECRET_KEYs
actions: Login on app_a (SECRET_KEY='key-alpha') to obtain a signed session cookie
GET /create on app_b (login_required endpoint) with the foreign cookie
expected: GET /create on app_b returns HTTP 302 redirect to /auth/login (session not trusted, user anonymous)
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

fd_a, path_a = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd_a)
app_a = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path_a, 'SECRET_KEY': 'key-alpha'})
with app_a.app_context():
    init_db()

fd_b, path_b = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd_b)
app_b = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path_b, 'SECRET_KEY': 'key-beta'})
with app_b.app_context():
    init_db()

def test_session_cookie_from_different_secret_key_rejected():
    client_a = app_a.test_client()
    r_login = client_a.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Anjali', 'password': 'cloud'})
    assert r_login.status_code == 302
    raw_cookie = r_login.headers.get('Set-Cookie', '')
    assert 'session=' in raw_cookie
    session_value = [p.strip() for p in raw_cookie.split(';') if p.strip().startswith('session=')][0]
    client_b = app_b.test_client()
    client_b.set_cookie('session', session_value.split('=', 1)[1])
    r_create = client_b.get('/create')
    assert r_create.status_code == 302
    assert '/auth/login' in r_create.headers.get('Location', '')

tests.name: test_default_dev_secret_key_overridden_by_config
preconditions: App created with explicit SECRET_KEY overriding the default 'dev' value
actions: Assert app.config['SECRET_KEY'] is NOT the default 'dev'
Assert app.config['SECRET_KEY'] equals the supplied value exactly
Login with valid credentials and confirm session cookie is issued
Confirm the session is valid by accessing a protected page

    assert r_login.status_code == 302
    cookie_header = r_login.headers.get('Set-Cookie', '')
    assert 'session=' in cookie_header
    r_create = client.get('/create')
    assert r_create.status_code == 200

tests.name: test_session_persists_across_requests_same_secret_key
preconditions: App created with TESTING=True and SECRET_KEY='persistent-key-99'
actions: GET /create — confirm 200 (session still valid across multiple requests)
expected: GET /create returns HTTP 200 (session cookie correctly re-verified each request)

from flaskr.db import init_db

tests.name: test_tampered_session_cookie_treated_as_anonymous
preconditions: App created with TESTING=True and SECRET_KEY='tamper-test-key'
actions: Login as James/river to get a valid signed session cookie
Manually corrupt the session cookie value by appending garbage bytes
Present the corrupted cookie to GET /create (login_required endpoint)
expected: GET /create with tampered cookie returns HTTP 302 redirect to /auth/login (signature invalid)
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path, 'SECRET_KEY': 'tamper-test-key'})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()

def test_tampered_session_cookie_treated_as_anonymous():
    client_good = app.test_client()
    r_login = client_good.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'James', 'password': 'river'})
    assert r_login.status_code == 302
    raw_cookie = r_login.headers.get('Set-Cookie', '')
    assert 'session=' in raw_cookie
    session_value = [p.strip() for p in raw_cookie.split(';') if p.strip().startswith('session=')][0]
    original_val = session_value.split('=', 1)[1]
    tampered_val = original_val + 'XXXXBADDATA'
    client_bad = app.test_client()
    client_bad.set_cookie('session', tampered_val)
    r_create = client_bad.get('/create')
    assert r_create.status_code == 302
    assert '/auth/login' in r_create.headers.get('Location', '')

tests.name: test_logout_clears_session_and_protected_page_redirects
preconditions: App created with TESTING=True and SECRET_KEY='logout-boundary-key'
actions: Login as Rahul/stone — confirm session active (GET /create returns 200)
GET /create after logout — confirm redirect to /auth/login (session cleared)
expected: GET /create after logout returns HTTP 302 to /auth/login
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path, 'SECRET_KEY': 'logout-boundary-key'})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()

def test_logout_clears_session_and_protected_page_redirects():
    client = app.test_client()
    r_login = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
    assert r_login.status_code == 302
    r_before = client.get('/create')
    assert r_before.status_code == 200
    r_logout = client.get('/auth/logout')
    assert r_logout.status_code == 302
    r_after = client.get('/create')
    assert r_after.status_code == 302
    assert '/auth/login' in r_after.headers.get('Location', '')
